sections.h2: Where are the Meade County property tax offices?
sections.html:
Both offices that matter share one address, 516 Hillcrest Drive in Brandenburg. The Property Valuation Administration (PVA) is in Suite 3, telephone (270) 422-2178, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The Sheriff's Office, which takes the payments, is in Suite 14 and answers at (270) 422-4937.

Think of the PVA as the office that decides what a property is worth, and the Sheriff as the office that collects on that figure. A homeowner with a question about an exemption or a value goes to Suite 3. A homeowner with a bill in hand goes to Suite 14. The County Clerk only enters the picture after April 15, when unpaid bills transfer to that office.

sections.h2: How do Meade County residents pay their tax bill?
sections.html:
Payment goes to the Sheriff. The 2026 bills were mailed on Friday, October 30, 2026, and the Sheriff's notice from November 4 acknowledged that many residents had not yet received them. The same notice pointed owners to an online property tax lookup so they could see the amount before the paper arrived.

  • By November 1: a 2 percent discount under KRS 134.015. Because the 2026 bills were mailed October 30, ask the Sheriff which schedule applies to them, since the statute allows an alternative schedule when mailing is delayed.
  • Through December 31: the printed amount.
  • January: a 5 percent penalty.
  • After January 31: a 10 percent penalty.
  • April 15: the last day to pay in person at the Sheriff's counter, which in 2026 meant 4:30 p.m.

One policy catches people out. The Sheriff stops accepting personal checks during the last two weeks of collection each year. Late payers then need cash, a debit or credit card, a money order or a cashier's check. The office says this is routine and not a permanent change.

sections.h2: What does a Meade County owner pay on a typical house?
sections.html:
The Census median value for an owner-occupied Meade County home is $207,900, above the $188,100 reported for McCracken County. At the state's 2025 rate of 10.6 cents per $100, the state share on that house is about $220.37. The county, the school district and other taxing districts set their own rates on top.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption in Meade County?
sections.html:
Yes. Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, receive a $49,100 reduction in assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. On the $207,900 median, taxable value becomes $158,800 and the state share falls to about $168.33.

The Meade County PVA set a filing date for 2026: applications were due May 22, 2026, so the exemption would show on the November bill. That date has passed, and owners who turn 65 in a later year should ask the office for that year's cutoff. The PVA says early filing also helps taxing districts estimate budgets and set rates. Bring a birth certificate, driver's license or passport as proof of age. Disability claims need a federal or retirement-system finding of total disability and, unless the owner is a service-connected veteran or has a Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems permanent finding, an annual renewal.

sections.h2: How does a Meade County owner appeal an assessment?
sections.html:
Meet with the PVA first. Kentucky allows an appeal only after that conference, and the PVA must explain the constitutional and statutory rules and how your value was set.

  • The tax roll is open for 13 days from the first Monday in May, and the PVA must advertise the dates.
  • File the appeal with the County Clerk by close of business on the day after the inspection period ends.
  • Prepare evidence on the land, buildings, insurance, construction cost and sale listings, since appeals without documents are denied.
  • Appear before the local board of assessment appeals, which meets 25 to 35 days after inspection ends and sits no more than five days without an extension.

Taxpayers may record the hearing audio. If your value is raised after bills are out, a supplemental bill follows for the difference.

sections.h2: What if Meade County taxes are still owed when the house sells?
sections.html:
The balance travels with the title. A delinquent bill becomes a certificate at the County Clerk after April 15, a lien is recorded, and 1 percent monthly interest begins. KRS 134.420 lets that lien run for 11 years whoever owns the property.

The county attorney mails a first notice within 30 days of the transfer and a second within 60 days. The sale date falls 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and the Clerk advertises the bills 30 to 45 days ahead. A third-party buyer who takes the certificate can add substantial fees. Ask the Sheriff for the payoff before April 15, and the Clerk after, and have the closing agent pay it from proceeds.

sections.h2: What is Meade County, Kentucky, like for a seller?
sections.html:
Meade County was formed in 1823 and covers 325 square miles, with the Ohio River marking all 56 miles of its northern edge across from Indiana. Much of the ground is karst plain dotted with sinkholes, and the northwest rises onto a plateau behind the Dripping Springs Escarpment. Brandenburg is the seat. Ekron and Muldraugh are the other cities, and Doe Valley and Fort Knox are census-designated places. Fort Knox is shared with Hardin County, and the county is part of the Louisville metro area, with easy access to the job centers at Elizabethtown and Fort Knox.

Most children attend Meade County Schools, whose high school is Meade County High School, while families living on Fort Knox are zoned to the Defense Department's school system. The county keeps Eastern time, and its western neighbors Breckinridge County and Perry County, Indiana, sit on the Central time line.

The mean commute is 33.0 minutes, 74.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and 91.5 percent of households have broadband. Poverty stands at 9.8 percent, against 13.9 percent in McCracken County. Sinkholes are common in the karst terrain, and a house with that kind of problem or with deferred repairs can slow a conventional sale. A cash buyer who purchases as-is can close without those fixes.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Meade County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Meade County Sheriff's Office, 516 Hillcrest Drive, Suite 14, Brandenburg, (270) 422-4937. The PVA in Suite 3 handles values and exemptions only.

faqs.q: When does the Meade County Sheriff stop taking personal checks?
faqs.a: About two weeks before the April 15 end of collection. After that point payment must be cash, card, money order or cashier's check.

faqs.q: What was the 2026 Meade County homestead filing date?
faqs.a: May 22, 2026, for the exemption to appear on the November bill. That date has passed, so ask the PVA about the next cutoff.

faqs.q: How much is the state share of tax on a $207,900 Meade County house?
faqs.a: About $220.37 at the 2025 state rate of 10.6 cents per $100. County and school rates are billed in addition.

faqs.q: What happens to Meade County bills unpaid after April 15?
faqs.a: They go to the County Clerk as certificates of delinquency. A lien is recorded, interest runs at 1 percent monthly, and a tax sale can follow 90 to 135 days after the transfer.
